title: Comparisons
subtitle: plus ... que, moins ... que, aussi ... que
summary: Compare people, things and the weather with plus, moins, aussi and autant, use mieux and meilleur, and meet être and avoir in the imparfait.

lesson.heading: The comparative at a glance
lesson.note: *Que* becomes **qu'** before a vowel: *plus chaud **qu'**hier*, *moins vite **qu'**Élodie*.

lesson.heading: More and less: plus, moins
lesson.text: Put **plus** or **moins** before an adjective or adverb, and **plus de** / **moins de** before a noun. After a verb, *plus* and *moins* stand alone. The second part of the comparison starts with **que**.

examples.text: Le TGV est **plus rapide que** le train.
examples.note: The TGV is faster than the train.
I have a lot more holiday than before.

examples.text: Ce train est **moins rapide que** le TGV.
examples.note: This train is slower than the TGV.
She has less free time than before.
They smoke a bit less than before.

lesson.heading: Equal: aussi and autant
lesson.text: Use **aussi** before an adjective or adverb, **autant de** before a noun, and **autant** on its own after a verb. Don't mix them up: ~~aussi de~~ and ~~autant intelligent~~ are wrong.

examples.note: He is as clever as his brother.
She drives as fast as before!

examples.text: Je n'ai pas **autant d'**amis **que** ma sœur.
examples.note: I don't have as many friends as my sister.
You work as much as I do.

lesson.heading: Better: mieux and meilleur
lesson.text: *Bien* and *bon* have their own comparatives. **Bien** (well, an adverb) becomes **mieux**; **bon** (good, an adjective) becomes **meilleur**, which agrees like any adjective. For the weather, say **il fait meilleur**.

examples.text: Ce film est **meilleur que** le précédent.
examples.note: This film is better than the last one.
She speaks German better than he does.

lesson.heading: More and more, same and different
lesson.text: **De plus en plus** and **de moins en moins** describe a change over time. To say two things are alike, use **comme**, **le même / la même**, **pareil** or **identique (à)**; the opposite is **différent (de)**.

examples.text: Papi, tu entends **de plus en plus** mal !
examples.note: Grandpa, your hearing is getting worse and worse!

examples.text: C'est **de mieux en mieux** ≠ **de pire en pire**.
examples.note: It's getting better and better ≠ worse and worse.

examples.text: Il fait **le même** temps **que** l'année dernière.
examples.note: The weather is the same as last year.
Today it's the same as yesterday.

examples.text: Ma mère est **différente de** ma tante.
examples.note: My mother is different from my aunt.

lesson.heading: A first look at the imparfait: être and avoir
lesson.note: The imparfait describes how things were in the past: *c'est → **c'était***, *il y a → **il y avait***. *Hier, l'eau **était** froide.* *Avant, nous n'**avions** pas d'ordinateur.*

lesson.text: Adjective or noun? Adjective → **aussi** (*aussi beau*); noun → **autant de** (*autant de livres*); verb → **autant** (*elle voyage autant*).

exercises.prompt: Il a ___ livres que ses parents.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun (*livres*), use **autant de ... que**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct form: Il fait ___ chaud que ce matin.
exercises.explanation: *Chaud* is an adjective, so no *de*: **aussi chaud que**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct form: Il y a ___ brouillard que ce matin.
Choose the correct form: Il fait ___ aujourd'hui.
exercises.explanation: *Bon* becomes **meilleur**; for the weather, say **il fait meilleur**.

exercises.prompt: Complete the expression: C'est de pire en ___ !
exercises.explanation: **De pire en pire** - worse and worse. The opposite is *de mieux en mieux*.

exercises.statement: Elle parle plus bien allemand que lui.
exercises.explanation: *Plus bien* does not exist: **Elle parle mieux allemand que lui.**

exercises.prompt: Complete each sentence with the missing word.

pairs.left: Ces deux verres sont ___ : on ne peut pas les distinguer.
Je vais prendre la ___ chose que toi.
Mes amis sont très ___ de moi.
Il fait plus chaud ? — Non, c'est ___ qu'hier.

exercises.prompt: Il y a du vent. → Hier, il y ___ du vent.
exercises.explanation: *Il y a* in the imparfait: **il y avait**.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence: "It's a bit less hot than yesterday."
exercises.answer: Il fait un peu moins chaud qu'hier.
